desc:
In one operation you choose an index i of arr and a position j of pool, and overwrite arr[i] with pool[j]. Pool values can be used any number of times, and the same index may be overwritten more than once (although that is never useful).

Return the minimum number of operations needed to make arr strictly increasing, or -1 if that is impossible. For arr = [1, 5, 3, 6, 7] and pool = [1, 3, 2, 4] the answer is 1 (replace the 5 with 2).
hints: Process the array from left to right. What is the only thing about the already processed prefix that matters for the future?
Only the value of the last element of the prefix matters (it must stay smaller than the next one). Keep a map from 'last value' to 'fewest operations used so far'.

For the next element x and each state (last, ops): keep x if x > last (cost ops), or replace it with the smallest pool value strictly greater than last, found by binary search in the sorted pool (cost ops + 1). The map never has more than len(pool) + 1 states. If it becomes empty, return -1.
editorial: Scan arr from left to right and keep best, a dictionary from the possible value of the last element of the processed prefix to the minimum number of replacements that achieves it. Initially the 'last value' is minus infinity with 0 operations.

For the next element x, every state (last, ops) has up to two successors. If x > last we may keep x: the new last value is x, cost unchanged. We may also replace x by the smallest pool value strictly greater than last (found with bisect_right on the sorted pool), at cost ops + 1. Choosing the smallest feasible pool value is optimal because a smaller last value can only make the future easier. When two paths reach the same last value, keep the smaller cost.

Every state's last value is either the current original element or a pool value, so there are at most len(pool) + 1 states per step. The total time is O(n · m log m) with n = len(arr) and m = len(pool), and memory is O(m). If at some point no states remain, the array cannot be fixed and the answer is -1; otherwise it is the minimum cost over the final states.
